name: FENRIS INDUSTRIAL GripMax HX Industrial Hand
product_name: FENRIS INDUSTRIAL GripMax HX Industrial Hand
description:
The GripMax HX is a wrist-terminated industrial hand replacement built for environments where tools fail and organic tissue has no business being. The frame is high-carbon steel with reinforced polymer knuckle guards, driven by hydraulic microactuators rated for 1,200 PSI crush force — enough to shear structural bolts or compress copper pipe fittings bare-handed. The palm houses a 400kg-rated electromagnetic array that can lock onto ferrous surfaces for climbing or cargo handling, switch to a repulsion mode for controlled component separation, and function as a magnetic tool holder during work. Fingertips are standardized hex-socket compatible, allowing direct drive of bolts without a wrench. The hand is deliberately overbuilt and visually industrial �� Fenris does not apologize for aesthetics.

The GripMax HX is the hand of choice for heavy industry, demolition, salvage, and deep-infrastructure maintenance crews who work in conditions that destroy lesser equipment. It is common in the Port Authority's hull-maintenance teams, the city's underground utility corridors, and anywhere the work involves metal, pressure, and the expectation of violence toward inanimate objects. On the street, it has found a second life among enforcers and debt collectors for whom the hand's capability communicates intent before a word is spoken.
installation_requirements: Wrist disarticulation, industrial-grade socket installation, standard surgical team sufficient; Fenris publishes open installation specs
rejection_risk: Moderate — hydraulic microactuator fluid has known inflammatory response risk in patients with autoimmune conditions; steel frame weight strains wrist socket over time without proper osseointegration
maintenance: Monthly hydraulic fluid check, quarterly electromagnetic coil inspection, annual socket torque assessment; replacement parts available at any industrial supply depot

side_effects: Significant wrist and forearm fatigue during extended use due to the hand's weight
Electromagnetic array interferes with nearby electronics and credit chips if not switched to standby
Users frequently underestimate crush force in social situations, crushing cups, handshakes, and door handles
Hydraulic fluid has a faint machine-oil smell that persists even after cleaning
cultural_context: A Fenris hand on the Shelf is a working tool, worn without ceremony. Among enforcers and street muscle, it has become a recognizable symbol of applied force — more honest than a weapon, because it is never put away.
known_users: Heavy industry and demolition workers, Shelf and Slab tiers
Underground utility and infrastructure maintenance workers
story_hooks: A series of industrial 'accidents' in a Port Authority maintenance crew all involve crush injuries inconsistent with equipment failure — someone's GripMax has been overclocked and someone else knows it
A Fenris GripMax recovered from a crime scene has a magnetic array that recorded a partial electromagnetic imprint of the last ferrous surface it contacted — enough to identify a location
The latest GripMax firmware update includes an undisclosed remote-disable feature that Fenris claims is for theft prevention, but which labor unions are calling a corporate control mechanism
